title: Waveform release scripting + pin scratchpad
content:
Purpose
- Scratchpad for a small hands-on rollout pattern I want to test: a timed "waveform" release that alternates small traffic pulses across cohorts while keeping a pinned fallback image for each cohort. More conservative than open canary; allows probing different client segments and load shapes.

Goals (what success looks like)
- No client-facing error rates >0.5% attributable to model/version change.
- P50 latency change <25ms, P95 <100ms compared to baseline route.
- Observability hooks capture at least: token-rate, model-version, error class, client-id, cohort, GPU memory pressure.
- Rollout script can be executed in <10 minutes by on-call and rolled back in <5.

High-level plan
1) Prepare artifacts
   - Build image: serving-runtime:2025.02.wave1 (already in registry)
   - Create pin config for cohort groups: pin -> image tag map in config-store
   - Create temporary rollout policy named waveform-wave-2025-02-14
2) Dry-run in staging (fast): run script with --dry-run, validate telemetry wiring and trace ids
3) Execute waveform in prod during quiet window (US-Early morning)

Cohort definition (for this experiment)
- cohort-a: internal-svcs (10% traffic)
- cohort-b: api-key-beta (5% traffic)
- cohort-c: mobile-android (2% traffic)
- control: remaining traffic (default image)

Waveform schedule (12 minute cycle repeated 6x)
- t=0: cohort-a -> new image (5 min), cohort-b,c control
- t=5: cohort-b -> new image (3 min), cohort-a back to pinned fallback
- t=8: cohort-c -> new image (2 min), cohort-b back to fallback
- t=10: all cohorts back to baseline, gap/pause 2 min for drift check
- repeat x6 (total ~72 min)

Safety thresholds (auto-abort)
- error-rate (4xx/5xx) increase > 0.3 percentage points vs baseline for any cohort for 2 consecutive 60s windows -> abort
- client-visible tail latency (P99) increases by >250ms for 2 consecutive 60s windows -> abort
- model-serving OOM or restart > 1 in any serving node -> abort

What to watch in dashboards (quick checklist)
- per-cohort error rate (annotation: compare to same cohort baseline)
- per-image token rate and free memory on GPUs
- trace sampling: find a few end-to-end traces from each cohort to confirm pathing and model-version header
- cost spike: tokens/sec * compute time (rough check)

Pinning notes (how to ensure fast rollback)
- always write pin map as atomic update: key = /releases/pins/waveform-2025-02-14, value = {cohortA:serving-runtime:2025.02.stable, cohortB:..., fallback:serving-runtime:2025.01.stable}
- pin update should be reversible with previous commit id (store previous pin in /releases/pins/history).
- When aborting, trigger 'force-pin' to map cohorts back to previous images immediately.

Example rollout script (pseudo)
- see below; keep idempotent and safe:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
RUN_ID=$(date -u +%s)-waveform
DRY_RUN=${1:-false}
# apply pin for cohort A
apply_pin() {
  cohort=$1
  image=$2
  echo "writing pin for $cohort -> $image"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "false" ]; then
    # CLI call to config-store (placeholder)
    rcfg write /releases/pins/$RUN_ID/$cohort "$image"
  fi
}

# sequence
apply_pin cohort-a serving-runtime:2025.02.wave1
sleep 300
apply_pin cohort-b serving-runtime:2025.02.wave1
sleep 180
apply_pin cohort-c serving-runtime:2025.02.wave1
sleep 120
# revert
apply_pin cohort-a serving-runtime:2025.02.stable
apply_pin cohort-b serving-runtime:2025.02.stable
apply_pin cohort-c serving-runtime:2025.02.stable

Observability smoke tests (manual quick checks)
- Query metrics: 
  - `sum by (cohort,version) (requests_total)` -> ensure traffic routing matches expected split
  - `rate(request_errors[1m])` filtered by cohort -> check for spikes
  - `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(latency_bucket[1m])) by (cohort,version)`
- Trace: open a trace from cohort-a and confirm response headers include `x-rw-version: 2025.02.wave1`

Abort / rollback playbook (fast path)
- On-call (first responder) tasks:
  1) Signal: `!abort-waveform RUN_ID` in #infra-rollouts (templated message)
  2) Run `force-pin --from /releases/pins/history/$RUN_ID/previous`
  3) Increase sampling for traces to 100% for affected cohorts for 10 minutes
  4) If OOMs persists, scale down concurrency on model-serving pool and throttle clients via rate limiters

Edge cases and open questions
- Edge: client-side sticky sessions may bypass cohort routing for long-lived connections -> need to validate with session-id sampling (TODO: add check)
- Q: Should we use region-level pins for multi-region clients? For now we limit to us-east-1 only.
- Q: Does the rollout script require a TTL on pins? Probably yes to avoid lingering pins if operator forgets to revert. Add TTL of 4 hours on pins.

Post-mortem / notes to self after run
- Collect representative request ids for each abort and save in run folder (/tmp/waveform-$RUN_ID/requests.txt)
- Short writeup: one-paragraph summary and whether metrics met goals
- Tag release in changelog: waveform/2025-02-14 -> outcome: success|abort

Short checklist for executing (one-pager)
- [ ] Slack sticky: notify #infra-rollouts and product-owners 30m before
- [ ] Validate staging dry-run (smoke traces + metric queries)
- [ ] Ensure on-call is scheduled and available for 90 minutes
- [ ] Run script in dry-run first, then live with RUN_ID recorded
- [ ] Monitor 0-10 min closely, be ready to abort
- [ ] If no issues after 60 min, escalate window to regular canary cadence OR promote image to stable

Notes to self (informal)
- This feels like a hybrid between micro-wave and canary; advantage: tests both short-lived spikes and longer tails.
- Keep the script small and observable-focused. Prefer human-in-the-loop for first 3 experiments.
- If stable after 3 waves, discuss automated cadence with Samira (ops) and Miguel (sre).

TODOs
- [ ] Add session-id sampling check to routing telemetry (ticket ENGINF-907)
- [ ] Add TTL to pin store and mirror to history automatically
- [ ] Convert pseudo script into real pipeline or runbook action

- JIRA: ENGINF-842 (rollout infra changes), ENGINF-907 (session sampling)

-- end of scratchpad --
